caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:pvc-9
attempts.entry_title: GABAA inhibition and plasticity of layer 4 synapses in guinea pig V1 (Saez and Friedlander 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's findings on blocking inhibition largely held up in this data, its finding that few cells change with inhibition intact held in part, and its input-mixing simulations could not be tested. With GABAA inhibition blocked by bicuculline, more cells changed after pairing, in both directions, and the spread of changes widened while the mean did not change. With inhibition intact, 25 to 35% of the measurable control cells were plastic against the paper's 14%, several control recordings are missing, and the lack of net change depends on an unstated choice of baseline sweeps. The simulations, arguing that inputs must be grouped almost completely by plasticity outcome, need the authors' single-cell stimulation data, which are not public.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Saez and Friedlander (2016) on CRCNS pvc-9, which holds whole-cell recordings of layer 4 cells in guinea pig visual cortex slices before and after a pairing protocol, with intact inhibition (current and voltage clamp) and with 2 uM bicuculline. It classifies each cell as LTP, LTD or no change, and compares the outcomes, mean changes and their spread between the groups. The single-cell stimulation data of the paper's Figure 3 are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Saez and Friedlander (2016) from CRCNS pvc-9

outcomes.statement: Plasticity was analysed in 28 control cells (14 in voltage clamp, 14 in current clamp) and 26 cells with 2 uM bicuculline in the bath.
outcomes.quote: We analyzed the plasticity outcomes in response to a Hebbian pairing protocol of L4 excitatory cell afferents using ECS in the absence (n = 28; n = 14 in V-clamp, n = 14 in I-clamp) and presence (n = 26, I-clamp) of 2μM bicuculline in the bath.
outcomes.notes: The Summary sheets of the data set mark exactly 14 VC, 14 IC and 26 bicuculline recordings as included and 11, 9 and 12 as excluded, the paper's numbers, and give a row and per-sweep amplitudes for each included cell. Every bicuculline test file is in voltage clamp (pA), as the Methods and Figure 2 say. The deposit holds complete recordings (baseline, pairing and post-pairing) for all 26 bicuculline cells but for only 10 of the 14 VC and 10 of the 14 IC control cells (a data_missing finding); this limits the control claims, not the count of cells the paper analysed. Changed from partially reproduced after round 1 of verification.
deviations: The counts of included cells come from the fill of the Summary sheets: every excluded row is red, as the data descriptor documents, and the included rows are unfilled (IC, VCB) or green (VC). Completeness is judged from the files.

outcomes.statement: With inhibition intact, few cells showed plasticity after pairing; 1 of 28 underwent LTP, 3 of 28 LTD and 24 of 28 no change.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C legend; Results, Extracellular stimulation, paragraph 1 (cited there as Fig 1A)
outcomes.quote: LTD cells (n = 3/28) are shown as blue bars; a single LTP cell (n = 1/28) is shown as a red bar; grey bars indicate cells whose strength did not change after pairing (n = 24/28).
outcomes.notes: No reading of (P) and (T) gives 1 LTP, 3 LTD and 24 NC. On the 20 complete control cells the readings give 1 to 3 LTP and 3 to 4 LTD, 5 to 7 plastic cells (25 to 35%, against 14% in the paper); the plastic VC cells are 3 LTD and 1 or 2 LTP of 10. Counting the seven missing cells whose sheet change is below 15% as NC, the counts out of 28 meet the partial criterion (plastic 2 to 6, NC within 2.4 of 24) under (a,a), (a,b), (c,a) and (c,b) if IC23 (sheet change -24.6%) is NC, giving 3 LTP, 3 LTD, 22 NC under (a,a), and under (c,b) if IC23 is LTD. The partial outcome exists only through this bound, and the bound is loose: of the 16 measured cells whose sheet change is below 15%, five (IC8, IC14, IC16, IC19, VC15) are plastic in some reading, two under (a,a). The sheets store no p values. With the first 120 baseline sweeps 8 to 11 of the 20 cells are plastic, mostly LTD. The 30 ms window, the alignment variants and a one-sided t-test give 5 to 7 plastic cells. IC13, LTP in some readings in the first version, now changes by -10.9% (sheet -12.8%) and is NC in every reading.
deviations: Eight of the 28 control cells have no complete recording in the data set; they are not measured. To judge counts out of 28, seven whose sheet change is below 15% in size are counted as NC (the paper's rule cannot make them plastic on the sheet's change) and IC23 is shown both ways.

The pre-pairing epoch is the last 120 baseline sweeps where a cell has more (assumed; see fig1-control-no-net-plasticity). Methods, Plasticity induction, "After the pre-pairing epoch was complete (120 stimuli at 0.2 Hz)".
Cells with two pairings (IC2, IC4, IC5, IC6, IC14) use the first pairing and the recording after it; the paper describes one pairing per cell (Methods, Plasticity induction).

Each sweep is aligned on the onset of the stimulus artifact (the first step at least a quarter of the largest step, within the 0.5 ms before it) and sweeps without a stimulus artifact are dropped (5 of 17319: four post-pairing sweeps of IC13 and one VCB19 sweep pinned at -2000 pA); both are corrections made after round 1 of verification. Aligning on the largest step, as the first version did, is shown as a variant.

The end of the stimulus artifact, which the claims file's measure (M) starts from, is found per file as the trough between artifact and response 0.5 to 3 ms after the stimulus (a standard choice); the stimulus is found per sweep because it moves to 87 to 99 ms in some sweeps of 10 files.
Every sweep with a stimulus is used; the paper's analysis used sweeps selected in its spreadsheets (green), by a rule the paper does not give.

outcomes.statement: Over the 28 control cells, pairing gave no net plasticity of EPSPs or EPSCs.
outcomes.quote: overall the pairing protocol resulted in no net plasticity of EPSPs (recorded under current clamp) or EPSCs (under voltage clamp) for the population of cells studied (n = 28; p>0.8, Student’s t-test, Fig 1A ).
outcomes.notes: On the 20 complete control cells the mean change is -2.6% to -3.4% and the one-sample t-test against 0 gives p = 0.27 to 0.44 in readings (P)(a), (b) and (c). With the first 120 baseline sweeps the mean is -12.3% to -13.3% and every reading reaches p < 0.05 (0.013 to 0.036), so the outcome rests on the choice of the last 120. Open question for the authors (see findings) on which baseline sweeps form the pre-pairing epoch.
deviations: Assumption: the pre-pairing epoch is the 120 sweeps before pairing where a cell has more (36 of 46 cells have more than 130). The Methods say pairing began "after the pre-pairing epoch was complete (120 stimuli at 0.2 Hz)", and the data set's sheets give pre-pairing means that match the last 120 sweeps (median difference 4.5% over 36 cells) and not the first 120 (24.3%). The first 120 are shown as a variant.
20 of the paper's 28 control cells.

Each sweep is aligned on the onset of the stimulus artifact (the first step at least a quarter of the largest step, within the 0.5 ms before it) and sweeps without a stimulus artifact are dropped (5 of 17319: four post-pairing sweeps of IC13 and one VCB19 sweep pinned at -2000 pA); both are corrections made after round 1 of verification. Aligning on the largest step, as the first version did, is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The mean change in PSR after pairing was -5.67 +/- 9.47% in voltage clamp, -1.41 +/- 10.92% in current clamp, and -3.53 +/- 10.26% over all 28 control cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Extracellular stimulation, paragraph 1; Figure 1B legend
outcomes.quote: The net change in the compound postsynaptic response (PSR) was -5.67±9.47% in V-clamp and -1.41±10.92 in I-clamp.
outcomes.notes: Under readings (P)(a) and (P)(c) the three means are within tolerance ((a) VC -3.25%, IC -2.46%, all -2.86%; (c) -4.03%, -2.68%, -3.35%) and the SD over cells (13.20% and 13.17%) is not (10.26 +/- 1.03); reading (b) misses the VC mean (-2.56%). The means are over 10 VC and 10 IC cells. With the first 120 baseline sweeps the means are -11.8% to -14.1% and none is within tolerance. The data set's sheets give, over all 28 cells, VC -3.14 +/- 13.40% and IC -5.79 +/- 9.51%, closer to the paper's values with the labels V-clamp and I-clamp exchanged; whether the paper exchanged them is asked of a reader (questions/saez-2016.yaml). With them exchanged the IC mean is outside tolerance in every reading and the claim would not be reproduced.
deviations: 20 of the 28 control cells; the last 120 baseline sweeps (assumed, as in fig1-control-no-net-plasticity); sweeps aligned on the artifact onset, as in fig1c-control-outcomes.

outcomes.statement: Voltage-clamp and current-clamp control outcomes did not differ; both were Gaussian, and their means and variances did not differ, so the two were combined.
outcomes.quote: both were Gaussian (p = 0.79 and p = 0.85 respectively, Shapiro-Wilks test) and their means and variances did not differ (p = 0.28, Student’s t-test; p = 0.61, Fisher’s F-test, respectively)
outcomes.notes: Under the adopted reading (P)(c) none of the four tests reaches p < 0.05: Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.68 (VC) and 0.20 (IC), t-test p = 0.83, F-test p = 0.59; (P)(b) agrees (smallest p 0.18). Under (P)(a) the Shapiro-Wilk test of the IC changes gives p = 0.0497, so the readings differ and, as the claims file says for claims of absence, the outcome is the one under the adopted reading. In the first version every reading agreed; the change came with the onset alignment and the dropped IC13 sweeps. The first-120 variant has no test below 0.05 in any reading.
deviations: 10 cells per clamp mode, not 14.

Assumption: where the readings of (P) disagree on a claim of absence, (P)(c), the last 120 post-pairing sweeps, is adopted. The Methods give "at least 10 more minutes of testing" after pairing; the 40 VC and VCB sheets that state it compared 120 traces ("Traces compared", 120); and of the two 120-sweep readings (c) is closer to the sheets' changes (34 of 46 cells within 5 points, median 2.0 points; (b) 30 of 46, 3.7 points).

outcomes.statement: In control cells the plasticity outcome did not depend on the initial synaptic strength, in current clamp or in voltage clamp.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F and 1H legend; Results, Extracellular stimulation, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Scatterplot showing lack of correlation between the initial recorded synaptic strength under I-clamp (EPSP) and the plasticity outcome (p>0.9). (G-H) As (E-F), for V-clamp experiments (p>0.1).
outcomes.notes: Pearson correlation of initial amplitude and change, IC r = -0.14 to -0.21, p = 0.56 to 0.69; VC r = 0.40 to 0.54, p = 0.11 to 0.26, over the readings of (P); Spearman (p of 0.19 or more) and the first-120 variant (p of 0.45 or more) also stay above 0.05. The paper's IC p > 0.9 is not matched.
deviations: 10 cells per clamp mode, not 14; judged in each reading of (P), as the claims file's rule for absence says.

outcomes.statement: A representative current-clamp control cell showed no plasticity (EPSP change -1 +/- 0.1%, p = 0.48).
outcomes.quote: Fig 1D shows a representative example I-clamp experiment in which no plasticity was induced (EPSP change = -1±0.1%, p = 0.48, Student’s t-test).
outcomes.notes: IC6 changes by -0.93% with t-test p = 0.47 under (P)(a), (T)(a), and by -1.06% with p = 0.41 under (P)(c). With the first 120 baseline sweeps IC6 changes by -22% and no IC cell matches.
deviations: IC6 is read from folder IC7, where its files are (the IC6 folder is empty); the files are the ones the IC6 sheet lists.
The last 120 baseline sweeps (assumed, as in fig1-control-no-net-plasticity).

outcomes.statement: With GABAA receptors blocked by 2 uM bicuculline, more cells changed after pairing (16 of 26), with outcomes of both signs; 7 of 26 underwent LTP, 9 of 26 LTD and 10 of 26 no change.
outcomes.source: Results, Extracellular stimulation in the presence of 2μM bicuculline, paragraph 1; Figure 2A legend
outcomes.quote: Under these conditions, a greater proportion of cells underwent changes in synaptic response after pairing (16/26, or 63%). There was heterogeneity in the sign of the plasticity outcome, with 7/26 (27%) of cells undergoing LTP ... and 9/26 (35%) of cells undergoing LTD ... In a third subset of cells, no significant change in the evoked EPSC occurred (10/26 or 38.5%
outcomes.notes: No reading gives 7, 9 and 10. Readings (a,a) (8 LTP, 9 LTD, 9 NC), (a,b) (7, 8, 11), (b,a) (8, 7, 11), (c,a) and (c,b) (7, 8, 11) meet the partial criterion; (b,b) has 6 LTD. Every reading has 14 to 17 plastic cells of 26, of both signs. The 30 ms window, the baseline ending 1 ms before the stimulus and a one-sided t-test give the same counts; aligning on the largest step gives 8, 8, 10 under (a,a). With the first 120 baseline sweeps the counts are 6 LTP and 11 to 14 LTD, outside the partial criterion.
deviations: The last 120 baseline sweeps (assumed, as in fig1-control-no-net-plasticity).

Each sweep is aligned on the onset of the stimulus artifact (the first step at least a quarter of the largest step, within the 0.5 ms before it) and sweeps without a stimulus artifact are dropped (5 of 17319: four post-pairing sweeps of IC13 and one VCB19 sweep pinned at -2000 pA); both are corrections made after round 1 of verification. Aligning on the largest step, as the first version did, is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Blocking GABAA inhibition raised the fraction of cells with plasticity from 4 of 28 to 16 of 26, showing that inhibition limits plasticity induction onto L4 cells.
outcomes.quote: With intact inhibition, a very small fraction of cells underwent a plastic change by our criteria (n = 4/28; LTP in 1/28 and LTD in 3/28 cells). This proportion was considerably increased when inhibition was abolished (n = 16/26; LTP in 7/26 and LTD in 9/26 cells)
outcomes.notes: In every reading the plastic fraction is larger in bicuculline (14 to 17 of 26) than in control (5 to 7 of the 20 measured; 5 to 8 of 28 with the missing cells bounded as in fig1c-control-outcomes). The bicuculline count is within 16 +/- 1.6 in every reading but (b,b) (14); the control count is never within 4 +/- 0.4. Fisher's exact test (variant) p = 0.002 to 0.096 against the bounded 28, p = 0.036 to 0.24 against the 20 measured cells.
deviations: Control counts as in fig1c-control-outcomes (20 measured, 8 bounded from the sheets); last 120 baseline sweeps (assumed).

outcomes.statement: In bicuculline, LTP cells changed by +39.9 +/- 14.7%, LTD cells by -38.5 +/- 20.4%, and NC cells by -3.0 +/- 7.6% on average.
outcomes.source: Results, Extracellular stimulation in the presence of 2μM bicuculline, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: 7/26 (27%) of cells undergoing LTP (average LTP EPSC change = +39.9±14.7%) and 9/26 (35%) of cells undergoing LTD (average LTD EPSC change = -38.5±20.4%). In a third subset of cells, no significant change in the evoked EPSC occurred (10/26 or 38.5%; average change = -3.0 ±7.6%)
outcomes.notes: In every reading but (b,b) the LTD mean (-32.6 to -36.6%) and NC mean (-3.4 to -4.6%) are within tolerance and the LTP mean (+78 to +87%) is not; (b,b) has only the LTD mean within. VCB17 changes by about +390%. Its response is real: before pairing its median trace has a 93 pA inward current 3 ms after the stimulus, after pairing 473 pA; the change is +408% from the median traces and +388% with a 50 ms baseline; and its sheet's amplitudes less the holding current give +390%, so the sheet's +62.9% includes the holding current. It is kept. Without it the LTP mean is +33.4 to +37.1%, within tolerance under (a,b), (b,a) and (b,b).
deviations: The last 120 baseline sweeps (assumed, as in fig1-control-no-net-plasticity).

outcomes.statement: The mean change over all cells did not differ between bicuculline (-3.8 +/- 34.3%) and control (-3.5 +/- 10.3%), but the variance of plasticity outcomes was significantly larger in bicuculline.
outcomes.source: Results, Extracellular stimulation in the presence of 2μM bicuculline, paragraph 1; Figure 1B and Figure 2B legends
outcomes.quote: whereas the mean EPSC change of all experiments (n = 26) was not different in the presence (-3.8±34.3%; average time plot shown in Fig 1B ) or absence (-3.5±10.3%; average time plot shown in Fig 2B ) of bicuculline (p = 0.97, Student’s t-test), the variance of synaptic plasticity changes was significantly increased in bicuculline compared to control (p<0.01, Fisher’s test)
outcomes.notes: In every reading of (P) the means do not differ (t-test p = 0.40 to 0.47) and the bicuculline variance is larger (F = 31 to 39, p below 0.01), so both tests hold, also with the first 120 baseline sweeps; the bicuculline mean (+10.2 to +13.0%) and SD (81.4 to 82.5%) are outside tolerance because of VCB17 (+390%, a real response; see fig2-subgroup-changes). Without VCB17 the mean is -1.8 to -5.0% and the SD 28.4 to 30.8%, the tests still hold, and the SD is outside tolerance in every reading. The data set's sheet values give -3.76 +/- 34.25%, the paper's numbers, with VCB17 at +62.9%.
deviations: The control group is 20 of the 28 cells.

outcomes.statement: Representative bicuculline cells underwent LTP (+59.4 +/- 26%, p < 0.001) and LTD (-37.6 +/- 19.9%, p < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Figure 2C and 2D; Results, Extracellular stimulation in the presence of 2μM bicuculline, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: For these connections, the change in strength was +59.4±26% for the LTP case (p<0.001, Student’s t-test; Fig 2C ) and -37.6±19.9% for the LTD case (p<0.001, Student’s t-test; Fig 2D ).
outcomes.notes: VCB29 changes by +56.1% (p = 5.0e-65, (a,a)) and VCB10 by -36.7% (p = 1.4e-34), with VCB7 also within the LTD tolerance, all p < 0.001; with the first 120 baseline sweeps the match holds under (P)(b). The sweep-to-sweep SDs of these cells are 18 to 24% of the pre-pairing mean, of the order of the paper's +/- values.

outcomes.statement: In bicuculline the plasticity outcome did not depend on the initial synaptic strength.
outcomes.source: Figure 2E and 2F legend; Results, Extracellular stimulation in the presence of 2μM bicuculline, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We did not observe a dependency of plasticity outcomes on initial synaptic response ( Fig 2E and 2F ; p>0.5).
outcomes.notes: Over the 26 bicuculline cells the Pearson correlation of initial EPSC and change is r = -0.14 to -0.16, p = 0.44 to 0.48 in every reading of (P); Spearman p = 0.74 to 0.89; the first-120 variant also stays above 0.05.

outcomes.statement: The cumulative distribution of plasticity outcomes of single-cell stimulation differs from that of ECS with intact inhibition, but not from that of ECS in bicuculline.
outcomes.source: Results, Mixing of unitary L4-L4 inputs, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: The cumulative distributions are different when the plasticity outcomes from SCS experiments were compared to the ECS experiments performed in regular aCSF (green line; p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), but not when compared to the ECS experiments with bath application of 2μM bicuculline (yellow line; p = 0.16, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).

statistics.n: 42 or 43 SCS connections and 28 control ECS cells
42 or 43 SCS connections and 26 bicuculline ECS cells

outcomes.notes: Needs the per-connection strength changes of the single-cell stimulation (SCS) experiments of the paper's reference 17. The data set holds only the ECS recordings and their sheets; the paper gives no location; the CRCNS bucket's pvc-1 to pvc-13 data sets were listed and only pvc-9 is by these authors. No public copy was found.

outcomes.statement: Simulated compound responses built by random mixing of unitary L4-L4 connections (18.05 +/- 6.19 inputs each) give a distribution of strength changes significantly narrower than both the ECS (bicuculline) and the SCS data, so random independent mixing would not produce the plasticity seen with ECS in bicuculline.
outcomes.source: Results, Mixing of unitary L4-L4 inputs, paragraph 1; Figure 3C; Methods, Input mixing simulation
outcomes.quote: We found that the distribution of SCR Δ N Strengths was significantly narrower than that of either ECS (p<0.001, Fisher’s F-test) or SCS (p<0.001, Fisher’s F-test) experimental data ( Fig 3C ).

statistics.about: SCR (S = 0) against ECS in bicuculline variances

outcomes.notes: Needs the SCS pre- and post-pairing strengths of reference 17, which are not public (see fig3a-ks-scs-vs-ecs).

outcomes.statement: Adding a segregation parameter S that biases each SCR's connections toward the plasticity class of the first, the SCR distribution broadens with S, and only for S of 0.9 or more does its variance not differ from that of ECS in bicuculline; segregation of inputs by plasticity state would have to be almost complete.
outcomes.source: Results, Mixing of unitary L4-L4 inputs, paragraph 1; Figure 3B and 3D; Methods, Input mixing simulation
outcomes.quote: We found that for most S values, the variance of the SCRs is lower (p≤0.05, Fisher’s F-test); only for values of S≥0.9 was there no significant difference in variance between the SCR and ECS Δ N Strength distributions (p>0.05, Fisher’s F-test).

statistics.about: SCR against ECS in bicuculline variances, S below 0.9 (printed as p≤0.05)
statistics.n: 26 SCRs and 26 ECS cells per S value

statistics.about: SCR against ECS in bicuculline variances, S of 0.9 and 1
statistics.n: 26 SCRs and 26 ECS cells per S value

outcomes.notes: Depends on fig3c-random-mixing-narrower and the SCS data of reference 17, which are not public.

findings.statement: Eight of the 28 control recordings that the Summary sheets mark as included are missing or incomplete. IC22, IC23, VC21 and VC25 have no folder (the archive has IC1 to IC21 and VC1 to VC17, while the sheets list IC1 to IC23 and VC1 to VC25). VC10 and VC17 end with the pairing file and hold no post-pairing recording. IC11's folder holds no post-pairing recording. IC7's listed post-pairing file 07305017 has no protocol name, no recording date and no evoked response at the usual time.
The IC6 folder is empty; the IC6 recording (files 07305007 to 07305011, as the IC6 sheet lists them) is in the IC7 folder, together with IC7's own files.
The IC11 sheet lists 07315003 (a single sweep) as the pairing and 07315004 as the post-pairing recording, but 07315004 is the 60-trial pairing file (protocol Extracellular pairing, 0.1 Hz).
The data descriptor says each recording is "triggered once every 10 seconds"; the test sweeps are every 5 s (0.2 Hz, as the paper's Methods say), and only the pairing trials are every 10 s.
Four derived files (VCB12_POST, VCB13_PRE, VCB13_Post, VCB15_PRE) state 10 kHz and 1 s sweeps in their headers; they hold the same 10000 samples per sweep as the 20 kHz, 0.5 s originals they copy.

The recording folders also hold derived copies of the recordings (Concatenate*, *_PRE, *_POST), whose sweeps are found one for one in the original files, and Clampfit .sta, .tmp and .bak files; the data descriptor mentions none of them. A user counting files would count recordings twice.

In seven files (of cells VCB7, VCB27, VCB30, VCB33 and VCB34) 26 to 89% of the sweeps have the stimulus at 87 to 99 ms, not at 107.9 ms as in nearly all other sweeps; the descriptor gives only "typically around 100 ms". A fixed analysis window misses these responses.

The sheets mark the sweeps used per cell (green) and give PRE and POST ranges such as 1-120 and 182-421, but nothing says which rule chose the sweeps or which files the ranges refer to; the VC and VCB sheets name no files. The VC and VCB sheets have a "p (one-tail)" label with no value, and the IC sheets none, so no per-cell p is stored. The amplitudes in the VCB17 sheet include the holding current, which the descriptor does not say.

The Summary sheets' per-cell changes reproduce the paper's bicuculline mean and SD (-3.76 +/- 34.25%, n = 26) but not its control values; the IC sheet gives -5.79 +/- 9.51% and the VC sheet -3.14 +/- 13.40% (n = 14 each), against the paper's I-clamp -1.41 +/- 10.92% and V-clamp -5.67 +/- 9.47%.

The VCB17 sheet computes the cell's change, +62.9%, from amplitudes that include the holding current (pre-pairing -579 pA, post-pairing -943 pA, on a holding current near -485 pA). Less the holding current they give -94 and -459 pA, a change of +390%, which the recording confirms (median traces 93 and 473 pA). The Summary sheet's +62.9% enters the bicuculline mean and SD that the sheets share with the paper (-3.76 +/- 34.25%).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1: the first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module pvc9.py and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier listed the CRCNS bucket for pvc-9 itself and tested peak_amplitudes and stimulus_indices on synthetic inputs. It had no attempt record.

disagreements.reason: The Summary sheets mark exactly 14 IC, 14 VC and 26 VCB cells as included, and 9, 11 and 12 as excluded, which matches the paper and the Methods. The VCB test files are in pA, so the bicuculline cells are voltage clamp. The archive holds complete recordings for only 10 IC and 10 VC of the 28 control cells; that limits the claims below, not this count. Inclusion is read from red fill only, green fill is never checked; the counts match the paper exactly, so this is low risk (point 5).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2: the full executed notebook of the author-revise-1 run, the helper module pvc9.py, the claims file and this record, with the paper's full text. Report in transcripts/saez-2016/verifier-2-report.md. The verifier agrees with all 16 outcomes and found no misreading of the paper in the claims file. It quoted six sentences the printed numbers do not support (cell 17 on VCB17, the record's fig2-mean response, the count of 342 sweeps, the count of 12 files, the sheet's LTP mean in the summary, and the README on assumed outcomes).

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. Most cells have more than 120 baseline sweeps (up to 400). Which 120 form the pre-pairing epoch? This attempt used the 120 just before pairing, which the Methods' wording and the sheets' pre-pairing means support; the first 120 change several outcomes (for control, 8 to 11 of 20 cells plastic and a mean change near -13% that differs from 0 at p < 0.05).

Question for the authors. The paper does not give the post-pairing window used for the change and the t-test (all post-pairing sweeps, the first 10 min, or the last 10 min), the form of the t-test (on sweeps or on 1-min bins; the sheets say one-tailed), the peak search window and baseline, or the rule by which sweeps were selected (the sheets mark selected sweeps in green). Each was run under every reading the claims file names; the classification counts change by up to 3 cells between readings. Where the readings of the window disagree on a claim of absence (fig1-vc-ic-same), this attempt adopted the last 10 min, as the sheets compare 120 traces and their changes are closest to that window.

It classifies each cell as LTP, LTD or no change, and compares the outcomes, mean changes and their spread between the groups. The single-cell stimulation data of the paper's Figure 3 are not in the data set.
